subject: A Chinese DRAM claim knocked 5.46% off the Kospi
bodyMarkdown:
I ended yesterday's issue telling you to watch Korean memory. It took one day. A Chinese company most people here have never heard of described a chip design at a conference on Saturday, and by Tuesday's close Korea's stock market was down 5.46 per cent.

## What CXMT actually said

ChangXin Memory Technologies, or CXMT, is China's biggest maker of **DRAM**, the fast working memory that sits beside a processor and holds whatever it is using at that moment. TechNode and TrendForce both reported on Monday that CXMT's president, Cao Kanyu, presented a new cell design at the Integrated Circuits and Chiplet Conference on October 10, and said the company will ship DDR5 server memory modules built on it by the end of this year. The design is **4F²**, meaning each memory cell takes up four times the square of the smallest feature the process can print, against the 6F² layout nearly everyone ships now. Stand the transistor upright and you save roughly a third of the area per cell. CXMT says it holds more than 300 patent families covering the architecture.

## What the claim cost in one session

The Seoul Economic Daily reported that Samsung Electronics closed down 7.39 per cent on Tuesday and SK Hynix down 10.09, pulling the Kospi down 5.46 per cent to 6,035 after it touched 5,911 intraday. The selling travelled. Reuters reported the Philadelphia semiconductor index fell 1.5 per cent, a fifth straight losing session and its lowest in about four weeks, with Micron down roughly 4.5 per cent during the day. Forbes pointed at a second trigger the same afternoon, Broadcom's chief executive Hock Tan comparing the current wave of AI spending to casino gambling. Some of it came back overnight. TradingKey reported the Kospi up 1.75 per cent in early Wednesday trading, Samsung up 3.34 and SK Hynix up 2.84.

## Why the reaction ran ahead of the facts

Here is my problem with Tuesday. CXMT gave a date and an architecture. It did not give speeds, capacities, yields or shipment volumes, and no customer has said it is buying. Those are the numbers that decide whether a memory product exists commercially, and they are the ones a company releases last when they are not good yet. The Korea Times reported CXMT is still working to stabilize yields on high bandwidth memory. Counterpoint Research put the company at about 8 per cent of global DRAM revenue in the first quarter, with other reporting closer to 10 per cent by September, so CXMT is real and it is growing fast. Growing fast and beating SK Hynix at server DDR5 within eleven weeks are two different claims, and only the first one got made on Saturday.

## The takeaway

Watch for a customer, not another conference slide. A named server maker qualifying CXMT's DDR5 would move me more than any architecture diagram, and none has. When Samsung and SK Hynix next report, listen to what they say about 2027 memory pricing, because that tells you whether they are treating this as a threat or as noise. And if you hold a US index fund you own Micron, so Tuesday was partly your loss, which makes this a reasonable morning to look at how much of your portfolio sits in one industry.
